metadata.category_rule: Ask: original self-posts with no external URL, excluding Show prefixes. Show: original title starts with Show HN or historical Show YC (case-insensitive). Algolia ask_hn/show_hn tags and unrestricted story searches retrieve checked candidates; unrestricted searches continue below each category cutoff, covering removed tags and edited titles. Candidates without a matching current category tag retain category_source=archive.
metadata.guide_basis: Chinese reading introductions written from original titles and available self-post excerpts, not linked articles or comment threads.
limitations: Only eligible stories from the supplied local archive; deleted/dead/untitled there are excluded.
Scores are query-time checked values, not month-end/final scores or historical HN front-page ranks.
Ask includes Tell HN, Launch HN and other self-posts, rather than only Ask HN-prefixed questions.
External index omissions can remain hidden by undercounted original scores; original and current channel categorization can differ.
Official missing descendants retains archive comments with explicit comments_source; kids length is not total comments.
Below-cutoff ID/time conflicts are excluded and listed in verification; ranking-affecting conflicts fail export.
First/last months are partial; early empty and sparse months remain explicit.

entries.title: Show HN: TikZ Editor – WYSIWYG editor for figures in LaTeX
entries.author: DominikPeters
entries.current_title: Show HN: TikZ Editor – WYSIWYG editor for figures in LaTeX
entries.excerpt: Hi all! TikZ is a widely-used LaTeX package for drawing figures in papers. It uses commands like \draw[->] (0,0) -- (1,2); to draw lines, shapes, text, etc. Academics usually code up their figures by hand, so there is lots of twiddling around with the coordinates and recompiling until things look nice. I guess it’s a bit like SVG, but it’s more code than markup, for example it has loops with \foreach. I built an open-source WYSIWYG TikZ editor (available for web and desktop)
entries.guide_zh: TikZ Editor 为 LaTeX 插图提供所见即所得编辑，减少手调坐标与反复编译。

entries.author: simedw
entries.current_title: Show HN: I trained a 125M model to autocomplete piano on-device
entries.excerpt: I trained a 125M-parameter transformer to autocomplete piano performances in real time (~108 notes/sec on an iPhone 15). The idea is basically GitHub Copilot or Tabnine, except instead of prompting it with code, you prompt it by playing a few notes on a MIDI piano. The model then continues what you played, entirely on-device. The app is free if anyone wants to try it. Happy to answer questions about the model, training, Core ML, or the many things that didn't work.

entries.excerpt: Hey HN, Henry from Cactus here! We got really great feedback here, and have now incorporated the suggestions to release Needle 2. The whole model is a single 14MB binary that runs a full session in 28MB of RAM; 45m parameters at 2bit compression. Needle hits 500 tokens/sec decode speed on a Raspber
entries.guide_zh: Needle2 将手机、穿戴设备与小型机器人的工具调用模型压缩到 14MB。
